question: The Governor’s emoluments are decided by the:
solution:
The correct answer is **__Parliament__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Governor is a titular head or constitutional head and at the same time, he is the agent of the centre as the union government nominates a Governor in each state.
 
• Part VI of the Constitution of India deals with the state Governors.
 
• The Governor is neither directly elected by the people nor indirectly elected by a specially constituted electoral college as is the case with the President.
 
• The Governor shall be entitled to such emoluments, allowances and privileges as Parliament may determine by law.
 
• The position, powers, and functions of the Governor in India are primarily mentioned in Articles 153 to 162 of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister**

 
 
• The Prime Minister (PM) is the** head of the Indian government**
 
• He is **responsible for overseeing the administration, implementation of policies, and execution of laws **passed by Parliament.
 
• The Prime Minister is usually the leader of the political party or coalition that has the majority of seats in the Lok Sabha (the lower house of Parliament).
 
 
 
• President :
 
 
• The President is the **ceremonial head o**f the Republic of India, representing the unity and integrity of the nation
 
• The Indian Parliament determines the pay for all elected officials, including Prime Ministers, Presidents, Vice Presidents, Governors, and MLAs. 
 
• The real executive authority is **vested in the Prime Minister** and the** Council of Ministers,** but** the President acts based on their advice (as per Article 74).**
